html:
The Yued, shown on the map as Yuat from 1600 to 1815, are a Noongar people of Western Australia, in the coastal plain and hills north of Perth around the Moore River.

Their neighbours were the Whadjuk to the south, the Ballardong to the east and the Amangu to the north. In 1846 Spanish Benedictine monks founded the mission town of New Norcia on Yued land. In 1918 the government opened the Moore River Native Settlement at Mogumber, where Aboriginal people, many of them children taken from their families, were held under harsh rules. Three girls escaped from it in 1931 and walked home along the rabbit-proof fence, a story later told in a book and a film.
